title: React Module 06 Applied Check
description: Apply form concepts to controlled/uncontrolled tradeoffs, numeric inputs, checkboxes, validation timing, async submits, and library decisions.
author: DailyCoder

questions.prompt: An input has `value={name}` but no `onChange`. What is the likely problem?

options.text: It becomes read-only from the user perspective

questions.explanation: A controlled input needs an update path. Without `onChange`, user edits cannot update the state value.

questions.prompt: A checkbox handler reads `event.target.value` and stores `"on"` instead of true or false. What should it usually read?
questions.explanation: Checkbox checked state is represented by the `checked` boolean.

questions.prompt: Which are good async submit practices? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Set a submitting flag while the request is in flight
Show field-level errors when the server returns field errors
Ignore rejected promises so users see nothing

questions.explanation: Async forms should communicate pending state, prevent duplicates, and surface errors clearly.

questions.prompt: Why is server validation still required when client validation exists?

options.text: Client validation can be bypassed and cannot enforce trusted rules alone
Server validation is only for styling
React prevents invalid network requests automatically

questions.explanation: Client validation improves feedback, but the server must enforce correctness and security.

questions.prompt: A file input should usually be treated as uncontrolled in React.
questions.explanation: Browsers restrict programmatic file input values, so refs or form submission APIs are typical.

questions.prompt: A numeric input stores `event.target.value`. What should you remember?

options.text: The value from the input is still a string unless you convert it
React automatically stores all numbers as BigInt

questions.explanation: Input values are strings from the DOM; convert when numeric logic needs a number.

questions.prompt: Which are signs that a form library may be worthwhile? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Many fields with repeated validation and touched/error state
Team-wide need for consistent form patterns

questions.explanation: Libraries add value when form state and validation patterns become repetitive or complex.

questions.prompt: A submit button remains enabled during a slow request. Users can click it repeatedly. What should you add?

options.text: A pending state guard and disabled UI while submitting
A random key on the button every render

questions.explanation: Pending state prevents duplicate submits and gives users feedback.
